assessments.reasoning: The prose requires a magic and version preamble followed by sections. The binary production gives the exact four-plus-four byte sequence. Noncustom sections are single-occurrence and ordered; repeating or interleaving custom sections is governed by separate custom-section entries in the production.

challenge.method: Read the Core 1.0 module production and current-engine controls for wrong version, duplicate type section, reversed type/import order and multiple custom sections. Compare Core 2.0’s added data-count section and binary version field.
challenge.results: The ordered base grammar and repeatable custom placements match the scoped claim and probes. The Core 2.0 snapshot adds data count while retaining binary version one. The binary header does not establish a language edition by itself.

limitations: This is the binary grammar in the December 2019 Recommendation. The numeric binary version field does not identify every subsequent language edition.
Exact dated publications govern the scope. The independently constructed current-engine cases are a supplementary challenge.
